The injury severity chapter shows trends in casualties by severity over recent decades. In 2025:

  • There were 1,538 reported road fatalities, 29,918 killed or seriously injured (KSI) casualties and 127,883 casualties of all severities.

  • Road fatalities remain substantially below historic levels (Chart 2). Fatalities have more than halved since 2004 and remain below pre-pandemic levels, with 2025 recording one of the lowest numbers of fatalities outside the pandemic period, a decline of 4% from 1,602 fatalities in 2024.

  • KSI casualties have fallen by around a third since 2004 (Chart 3). However, most of this reduction occurred before 2010 and KSI numbers have remained relatively stable over the past decade, excluding the period affected by the pandemic. The 2025 figure was an increase of 4% from 28,876 in 2024.

  • Casualties of all severities have fallen by over half since 2004 (Chart 4). Unlike fatalities and KSI casualties, the long-term decline in all casualties has remained relatively steady, though 2025 showed little change from 128,272 in 2024.

  • Casualty rates per mile travelled have generally declined over time. This indicates that improvements in road safety have occurred despite long-term growth in traffic volumes. In 2025, there were 4 fatalities, 86 KSI casualties and 369 casualties of all severities per billion vehicle miles travelled.

  • Data from police forces using injury-based reporting systems show that most casualties are classified as slight injuries, while less serious injuries account for the majority of serious injuries. More severe injuries such as fractures, internal injuries and serious head injuries are less common but represent a substantial proportion of serious casualties.
